name: Absent Bansho (Yakuza Archetype)
body:
The life of a yakuza can be dangerous, and taking the risks required to be loyal to a gang can threaten one’s life. An absent bansho is one who has learned how to avoid sticking their neck out, often by creating a second identity to draw attention and potential retaliation away from their true identity.

Second Life (Ex)

At 1st level, an absent bansho gains the dual identity and seamless guise vigilante class features, although both class features are treated as their social identity. As long as an absent bansho does nothing to hint that the two identities are related, they are treated as though they were two different people for the purpose of the dual identity class feature. This ability replaces contacts and gang war.

Loose Alliance (Ex)

An absent bansho gains the gang war class feature at 5th level and gang leader at 13th level, and they treat their yakuza level as if it were 4 levels lower for all effects related to these abilities. They do not gain the gang warlord class feature at all. This modifies gang war, gang leader, and gang warlord.

Vigilante Talents (Ex)

At 2nd level, an absent bansho gains a vigilante talent treating their yakuza level as their vigilante level. They are also treated as though they had the stalker vigilante specialization, and treat sneak attack as though it was sudden strike for the effects of vigilante talents. At 8th level and again at 15th, they can select an additional vigilante talent. This ability replaces the gang abilities gained at 2nd, 8th, and 15th level.

Clan Mage

Yakuza tend to focus on more mundane things, leaving the mystic arts to others. But for clan mages, these secret arts are passed down along with more esoteric tricks.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

A clan mage can cast ninja spells while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. Like any other arcane spellcaster, a clan mage wearing medium armor, heavy armor, or a shield incurs a chance of arcane spell failure if the spell in question has a somatic component. A multiclass clan mage still incurs the normal arcane spell failure chance for arcane spells received from other classes.

Spell Casting

A clan mage casts arcane spells as a legendary ninja, also using tattoos as though they were a legendary ninja and can ignore spell components. Yakuza use Charisma to determine which spells they can cast and bonus spells received from a high casting ability score.

This ability replaces the no trace class feature, the uncanny dodge class feature, and the 5th, 11th, and 17th level sneak attack increase.
